  AGENDA

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business
hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make
inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the
Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours
prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however,
to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a
presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council must
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits
the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific
agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City
Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of
items shown on the agenda.

separate discussion. Any item removed from the Consent Agenda will be considered immediately
following the motion to approve the Consent Agenda.

1.  Minutes of City Council Meeting of March 23, 2010

  Recommendation: Review and File.

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

3.  Resolution R10-05: Adjusting the FY 2009-10 Budget and Approving Use of General Fund
  Balances to Reduce the City’s CalPERS Safety Plan Side Fund Liability

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R10-05,
  adjusting the FY09-10 budget and approving the use of general fund balances,
  designated and undesignated in excess of 50% targeted balance, to reduce the
  CalPERS Safety Plan side fund liability.

4.  Extension of Tree Trimming, Landscape Maintenance, and Weed Abatement/Fire Safety
  Contracts through FY 2010-11

  Oakridge Landscape, Inc., through FY10-11.

5.  PW-557B-09; Completion of Contract for the FY 2009-10 Overlay Project

  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council accept as complete the
  construction contract PW-557B-09, FY09-10 Overlay Project in the amount of
  $530,868.85; and direct the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion, and release the
  10% retention 30 days after the County Recorder’s office records the Notice of
  Completion, if no stop notices are filed.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  April 13, 2010

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Perkins.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Perkins, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Rea,
  Mayor Humphrey

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Pannone, Assistant City
  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, Administrative Analyst Davis,
  Minutes Secretary Monson

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Humphrey asked Police Chief Dreiling to convey the Council’s congratulations to Services
Officer Jaylin Albao and also to John Douglass, the City’s disaster preparedness coordinator. Both
were mentioned in the March issue of Peninsula People – Ms. Albao for receiving the Employee
Recognition Award from the Police Officers’ Association and Mr. Douglass for his work in emergency
preparedness both locally and nationally.

Mayor Humphrey announced that Ed Ritscher, former City Treasurer and Councilmember (29 years of
service), was nominated by the City and has received the Older Americans Recognition Day Award
from Los Angeles County Commission for Older Adults. Mr. Ritscher will receive the award at a
ceremony on May 19th at the Hall of Administration downtown.

CONSENT AGENDA

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and unanimously
approved that the following Consent Agenda items be approved:

•  MINUTES OF CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF MARCH 23, 2010

•  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT – MARCH 2010

CITY COUNCIL
APRIL 13, 2010  1
 •  ADOPT RESOLUTION R10-05; ADJUSTING THE FY 2009-10 BUDGET AND
  APPROVING USE OF GENERAL FUND BALANCES, DESIGNATED AND
  UNDESIGNATED IN EXCESS OF 50% TARGETED BALANCE, TO REDUCE THE
  CITY’S CALPERS SAFETY PLAN SIDE FUND LIABILITY

•  EXTEND THE TREE TRIMMING CONTRACT WITH TRAVERS TREE SERVICE, INC.,
  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE CONTRACT WITH MERCHANTS LANDSCAPE
  SERVICES, INC., AND WEED ABATEMENT/FIRE SAFETY CONTRACT WITH
  OAKRIDGE LANDSCAPE, INC., THROUGH FY10-11.

•  ACCEPT AS COMPLETE THE CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT PW-557B-09, FY09-10
  OVERLAY PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $530,868.85; AND DIRECT THE CITY
  CLERK TO FILE THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION AND RELEASE THE 10%
  RETENTION 30 DAYS AFTER THE COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE RECORDS THE
  NOTICE OF COMPLETION, IF NO STOP NOTICES ARE FILED.

•  APPROVE THE SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE AMERICAN DIABETES
  ASSOCIATION “TOUR DE CURE” TO BE HELD ON SUNDAY, MAY 2, 2010

•  APPROVE THE SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE PALOS VERDES
  MARATHON TO BE HELD ON SATURDAY, MAY 15, 2010

•  PARKLANDS COMMITTEE MEETING ITEM OF MARCH 8, 2010

  PC-309-10; APPLICATION TO REMOVE ONE CAMPHOR TREE IN THE CITY
  PARKWAY LOCATED ADJACENT TO 4105 VIA NIVEL
  APPLICANT: MICHAEL G. AND TAMMY HINES
  ACTION: APPROVED

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Camille Feldman, [PVE Resident], asked the Council to vigorously defend the City against the lawsuit
filed by the School District regarding rezoning Lots C & D. She believes that the School District
would aggressively market the property if the zoning changes were agreed to. She believes changing
the zoning would set a precedent for all the other properties that have been deeded to the School
District by the Palos Verdes Homes Association. She does not want to see the “dismantling” of the
City’s CC&Rs.

DEMANDS

CITY COUNCIL
APRIL 13, 2010  2
 It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and seconded by Councilmember Bird that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council, totaling $230,126.93 be allowed and it was
unanimously approved.

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and seconded by Councilmember Bird that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council, No. 517174V, 517240H to 517243H, 517244 to 517352
totaling $236,861.96 be allowed and it was unanimously approved.

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS – none

CLOSED SESSION: Council recessed to Closed Session at 7:45 p.m.
  • PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Title: City Attorney
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957

RECONVENE: Council reconvened at 9:45 p.m.

The Council unanimously decided to appoint Christi Hogin, of the firm Jenkins & Hogin, as City
Attorney for the City of Palos Verdes Estates, subject to approval of a contract at the next meeting.
The Mayor called a special meeting for 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, April 17, 2010 in Palos Verdes Estates
City Council Chambers to consider the contract.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business before Council the meeting was adjourned at 9:50 p.m. to Saturday,
April 17, 2010, at 8:30 a.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall for the purpose of a Special
Meeting to discuss the City Attorney contract.

  RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED,

  MICHÉLE D. MONSON, MINUTES SECRETARY

APPROVED:

ROSEMARY HUMPHREY, MAYOR

CITY COUNCIL
APRIL 13, 2010  3
